significance: A gurdwara at Agra dedicated to the memory of the ninth Guru, Tegh Bahadur, built in the 1970s through the efforts of Sant Baba Sadhu Singh Mauni beside a red sandstone reservoir of 1610 raised in Jahangir's reign for water conservation. Eight of the tank's original twelve towers survive, their carving akin to Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri.
story: Sikh tradition holds that it was here that Guru Tegh Bahadur laid down his arms and offered himself for arrest before his martyrdom.
